     feature-card prose back into the brief instead of the reference doc
     (largest single-commit deltas: +6.6k B SA-0MVPZGAU5001FDO3, +4.1k B
     80dbf5a23 stash-hygiene, +3.1k B 19db86445 gate-failure docs, +3.0k B
     a624d18ed outbound-edge gate, +2.1k B each drive and per-child lock).
2. **The largest inline blocks are deep reference material, not operational
   steps.** The `## Steps` section alone is 45.5k chars (~11.4k tok):
   - `6.1 Parent recursion` — **19,068 chars (~4.8k tok)** — drive/parent
     orchestration, per-child locks, failure-recovery tiers, guard tables
   - `9. Commit, Push and mark in_review` — **11,079 chars (~2.8k tok)** —
     push timeout, terminal-status read-back, gate-failure reason tables
   - `### When finish refuses` — **7,202 chars (~1.8k tok)**
   - Background Job Etiquette — 3,927 chars; StatusLifecycle Integration —
     2,785 chars; gate-failure `reason`/facts — 3,142 chars
3. **The deep detail already lives in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
   (82,844 B) but the SKILL.md body duplicates it inline** instead of linking
   to it. The F5 "operational brief + deep docs" pattern was abandoned.
4. **No regression gate exists on SKILL.md *body* size.** The context-budget
   gate (`measure_context.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, tests
   `test_context_budget_gate.py`) only measures AGENTS.md files and the
   skills-section *description prose* (`skills_prose` = frontmatter
   `description:`), **not** the `SKILL.md` bodies loaded on invocation. The F5
   budget was a one-shot trim with no ongoing enforcement, so the file could
   silently regrow.
5. **Secondary: the system prompt contributes ~5.3k tokens** (measured 21,080
   chars in a real session) — dominated by `project_context` (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md
   ~3.2k tok + project AGENTS.md). Projects with very large AGENTS.md (e.g.
   AI_Hell system sections = 45,416 chars ≈ 11.3k tok) push near-miss sessions
   over the threshold without any skill change.
6. **The 216k–452k sessions are a separate failure mode** — resumed/hydrated
   sessions where the implement turn arrived after a huge *accumulated*
   context (the tables mark them as such). Not caused by SKILL.md alone, but a
   small SKILL.md body reduces the burn rate toward that failure.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — runs `/skill:implement` on work items; the local
  proxy must accept the turn's context. A 25k baseline with near-miss at 38k
  is too close to the edge and growing (sessions already exceed 200–450k).
- **Agents** — every implement turn pays the fixed ~19k-token cost of the
  SKILL.md body before doing any work; a smaller brief loads faster and leaves
  more headroom for the work itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` is reduced to **≤ 20,000 B** (measurable with
   `wc -c`), a ≥74% cut from the current 76,286 B, restoring the F5
   "operational brief" size class (F5 budget was ≤15,453 B).
2. Every removed/abridged section is preserved — verbatim or summarised with a
   link + SA reference — in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (or an
   appendix there), so no behavioural content is lost (F5 AC2 pattern).
3. The brief still documents every command/flag an operator needs to run the
   workflow end-to-end (worktree creation, `implement.py start/finish/parent/
   drive`, `wl` status transitions, StatusLifecycle, push-to-dev); workflow
   semantics are unchanged.
4. A **regression gate on SKILL.md body size** is added so the file cannot
   silently regrow: extend `measure_context.py` (or the context-budget gate /
   a dedicated test) with a `skill_implement_md` byte threshold committed in
   `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, enforced by the pre-push hook
   and a test — mirroring how AGENTS.md sizes are already gated.
5. Tests asserting SKILL.md content are updated and passing:
   `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_tdd.py`, `skill/implement/tests/` etc. — content that
   moved to the reference doc must be asserted against the reference doc
   (F5 AC4 pattern: "SKILL.md-content tests updated to check the reference
   docs").
6. **Measured context reduction:** rerunning the composition measurement shows
   a cold implement turn at ≤ ~6.5k tokens from the skill body (down from
   ~19k), documented as a before/after in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` or the
   implement reference doc.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The `## Steps` operational sequence (1–9) and its gating semantics must
  survive; only deep reference prose (rationale, tables, guard matrices,
  failure-mode taxonomies, SA-tagged feature cards) moves to the reference
  doc.
- Do **not** relax safety content (dirty-tree gate, worktree isolation,
  abort/reset, terminal-status guarantees) — preserve it verbatim or with a
  direct link.
- The implement skill's `tests/` must stay green; doc-content tests that pin
  moved prose must be repointed to the reference doc, not deleted.
- Keep the hidden-skill invocation map and extension conventions intact
  (`extension.json`, `SKILL_PREFIX/POSTFIX.md`).
- No change to `implement.py` runtime behaviour — this is a documentation/
  context-surface change only (SKILL.md + gate + reference docs + tests).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — 76,286 B / 75,774 chars / ~19k tokens, inlined
  on every implement invocation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — 82,844 B, already holds deep
  reference material (drive recovery, per-child lock, worktree removal,
  finish guards, push timeout, terminal read-back).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` + `context-budget.thresholds.json` — startup
  static-context gate; measures AGENTS files + description prose, **not**
  SKILL.md bodies.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — the canonical measurer;
  needs a SKILL.md-body component for AC4.
- Session evidence: cold implement turns at P50 ≈ 24.2k tokens (skill body
  75,774 chars/4 ≈ 18.9k + system ≈ 5.3k); near-miss 38,298–38,752; giant
  sessions 216k–452k (resumed/hydrated — separate failure mode noted in ACs/
  risks).

## Desired change

- Shrink `skill/implement/SKILL.md` back to an operational brief ≤20 KB by
  relocating the seven largest deep blocks (6.1 Parent recursion, Step 9
  push/commit detail, `When finish refuses`, gate-failure reason tables,
  Background Job Etiquette, StatusLifecycle Integration, worktree
  creation detail) to `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, leaving a
  link + one-paragraph summary each.
- Add a byte-size regression gate so this can never silently regrow again.
- Document the before/after context composition.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the file to shrink (76,286 B → ≤20,000 B).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — destination for relocated deep
  prose (already 82,844 B, has the matching sections).
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — add a `skill_implement_md`
  (or per-skill body) measurement component for the regression gate (AC4).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — commit the new byte threshold.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — enforce the new threshold (AC4).
- `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`,
  `tests/test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py` — extend for the body-size
  gate.
- Content-pinning tests — `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_tdd.py`,
  `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py`, `skill/implement/tests/`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — document the before/after cold-turn
  composition (AC6).

## Related work

- **SA-0MSLK7SAE0032V9K** — F5: "Trim six largest SKILL.md files by ≥30%"
  (completed). Established the ≤15,453 B implement budget this item restores;
  its AC2/AC4 patterns are the template for this work.
- **SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF** — audit SKILL.md restructure to operational brief +
  deep docs (completed) — the pattern for "brief + reference-doc" splitting.
- **SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS** — epic: "Reduce initial LLM context from skills and
  skill-related startup files" (completed). Its F1 tooling (measure_context.py)
  and F6 regression gate are the machinery reused here.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size
  (duplicate AGENTS.md + skills section)" (completed) — same class of problem
  for audit.
- **AGENTS_GLOBAL.md / AGENTS.md context budget** — startup surface (~5.3k tok
  system prompt) is the secondary contributor; projects with very large
  AGENTS.md (AI_Hell ≈ 24 KB) amplify near-miss sessions. Out of scope for this
  item but noted as a constraint/risk.
- **SA-0MTT7EUH30054I41** — compaction config for the Local Proxy fallback
  path (client-side compaction disabled) — relevant to the giant 200k–452k
  hydrated-session failure mode, tracked separately, not fixed here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** the same bloat affects other skills (audit 64.1 KB, ship
  33.8 KB, plan 27.2 KB, intake 21.5 KB, test 20.4 KB). This item is scoped to
  implement only; sibling trims should be separate work items. Risk: an
  operator may expect all skills trimmed at once — the ACs pin implement only.
- **Regression gate ≠ guarantee:** a body-size gate prevents silent regrowth
  but every *intentional* addition must flow through the gate (regenerate
  thresholds with justification, as AGENTS.md bumps do). Decide one
  threshold: F5-budget (15,453 B) vs "brief" allowance (20 KB) — AC1 proposes
  20 KB with F5 as reference. (Choose 20,000 B — see AC1; can be lowered after
  acceptance to the exact F5 figure if the brief compresses further.)
- **Resumed/hydrated giants (216k–452k):** not fully fixable by SKILL.md size
  alone — accumulated context across a long session is the driver. ACs
  intentionally exclude this; a smaller body reduces burn rate toward it but a
  separate work item may be needed for session-hydration limits.
- **Content-pinning tests:** some tests assert exact prose in SKILL.md; the
  almost-verbatim overlap check found ~0% shared lines with the reference doc,
  so moved prose will need deliberate re-pinning in tests — budget for it.
- **Assumption:** a ~19k-token body is the primary lever (78% of a 24.2k cold
  turn; 4.9× over the F5 budget) — verified by direct measurement of the file
  and real session logs on this machine.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metric defines the problem — P50 cold-start tokens, the 38k
  near-miss threshold, or the 200k–452k hydrated sessions?" — Answer
  (operator, seed context): "At P50 we are around 25k which is right on the
  edge of what can be accepted locally. We need to get this down." The 5
  largest sessions are explicitly "resumed/hydrated — the implement turn
  arrived after a huge accumulated context"; the 38k cluster is the
  near-miss population. Source: intake seed + session tables (2026-11-01).
  Research: verified cold-turn composition = SKILL.md body (~19k tok) +
  system sections (~5.3k tok) ≈ 24.2k, matching P50 ≈ 25k. The giant-session
  mode is a separate failure tracked in Risks.
- Q: "Is a regression gate (AC4) in scope, or just the trim?" — Answer
  (intake inference from F5/F6 precedent + 'get this down'): a gate is
  required — without it the F5 trim (which had a budget that was never
  enforced) simply repeats. Marked AC4; if the operator wants the trim only,
  AC4 can be dropped without weakening ACs 1–3/5–7. OPEN QUESTION: confirm
  the 20,000 B allowance vs the exact F5 15,453 B figure.

# A no-op finish finalised an item whose acceptance criteria were unmet

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` marks a work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal) even
when its worktree produced **no commit attributable to the item** and its
acceptance criteria were never exercised (e.g. an operational run that must
happen on its own schedule). On that no-op path the report attributes the
ambient `dev` HEAD — a hash belonging to a *different* work item — as "the
commit", so a parent whose child carries zero work is advanced to `in_review`:
a silent false positive that hides unmet ACs from the producer and the audit
skill.

## Users

- **Driven child sessions / agents**: a session whose worktree is clean
  (first session died before writing, or the item legitimately waits on an
  external window) must never see its item silently finalised with no work.
- **Producers / operators**: must be able to trust `in_review` — it means the
  ACs are actually met. A false `in_review` hides outstanding criteria.
- **Audit skill**: reads terminal state to decide what to verify; a false
  terminal hides a genuinely unmet AC5-style operational criterion.
- **Verification-only items** (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): items whose only
  deliverable is *running* a measurement and recording evidence — the
  legitimate no-op-push path must keep working, now behind an explicit signal.

### User stories

- As a producer, when a child was finalised with zero commits and no
  acceptance evidence, I want the item to stay open with a loud explanation,
  so `in_review` never hides unmet ACs (the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM cascade is
  impossible).
- As an agent running `finish`, when I legitimately complete a
  verification-only item with no code change, I want an explicit
  `--verification-only` flag that finalises it and reports "no changes, no
  commit" — never a commit hash belonging to someone else's work.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — No-op finish refuses the terminal write by default.** When
  `phase_finish` detects its worktree produced no commit attributable to the
  item (clean-tree/no-diff path) and no `--verification-only` signal is
  present, it must **not** write `status=completed`/`stage=in_review`: the
  item stays in its prior state, `finish` fails (or reports loudly) with an
  actionable message, and no "Implementation complete. Commit \<sha\>" comment
  is posted using an ambient/unrelated HEAD.
- **AC2 — Commit attribution is never false.** `finish`'s completion report
  may only name a commit that is attributable to this item (created by this
  finish run or a prior run of this item's worktree). On the no-commit path it
  must say "no changes / no commit", naming the retained worktree and any
  recorded evidence instead of the ambient `dev` HEAD.
- **AC3 — Verification-only path preserved behind an explicit flag.** An
  explicit opt-in (e.g. `implement.py finish <id> --verification-only`) still
  finalises a no-commit item to `completed`/`in_review`, exactly preserving
  the behaviour pinned by `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`
  (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): terminal status persists and the store read-back
  assertion still passes, but the report names "no changes" and never
  misattributes a hash.
- **AC4 — drive/phase_parent never presents zero work as finishable.** A child
  whose worktree exists but carries no commit attributable to the item and no
  verification-only signal is classified as "no work / not finalisable":
  `drive`/`phase_parent` does **not** run `finish` on it, reports it as such
  (child stays open), and the parent is **not** advanced to `in_review`.
  Finish's own refusal (AC1) remains the defence in depth for direct
  invocation.
- **AC5 — Automated regression coverage.** Unit/integration tests cover:
  (i) commit-vs-no-op distinction in `git_commit`, (ii) the default refusal
  path (AC1), (iii) the `--verification-only` path (AC3) including the
  existing no-diff status regression pin, and (iv) the drive/phase_parent
  classification (AC4).
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (and any related
  implement-skill docs) documents the new no-op semantics, the
  `--verification-only` flag, and how the agent should treat a clean,
  commit-less worktree.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Preserve the deliberate no-op-push path** (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): the
  regression pin `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` must
  continue to pass — verification-only items must remain finalisable, now only
  via the explicit signal (per the producer's decision).
- **Lifecycle invariants unchanged**: `StatusLifecycle` remains the only
  writer of status/stage; assignee release on completion is unchanged; the
  terminal read-back assertion (`_assert_terminal_status`) stays as the
  fail-loud guard.
- **Deterministic, machine-checkable gating**: no free-text/heuristic evidence
  parsing as the gate for the no-op path — an explicit flag carries it
  (producer decision Q2).
- **Surgical change**: no new flags or behaviour outside `implement.py finish`
  and `drive`/`phase_parent` classification unless required by the ACs.

## Existing state

- `git_commit` (lines ~2961) returns `True` both when it commits and when the
  tree is clean ("No changes to commit (clean working tree)"), so
  `phase_finish` cannot distinguish a real commit from a no-op.
- After `git_commit`, `phase_finish` reads `git_get_commit_hash(worktree_path)`
  (the branch HEAD — for a clean, commit-less worktree this is the ambient
  `dev` HEAD, i.e. someone else's commit), pushes the identical branch as a
  no-op, and `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes
  `status=completed`/`stage=in_review`. The completion comment reports
  "Implementation complete. Commit: \<ambient HEAD\>".
- `_assert_terminal_status` (lines ~707) only verifies the store *held* the
  terminal write — it cannot distinguish "finished work" from "nothing to do".
- `drive`/`phase_parent` (lines ~9240–9320) run `finish` whenever
  `_has_worktree_changes` is truthy; a clean-but-present worktree is reported
  as "worktree exists … implement, then re-run", but the no-op finish path
  above still finalises a commit-less child when it is reached (observed
  2026-11-01T12:55Z).
- The observed incident: `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1` was flipped
  completed/in_review with zero work; its parent `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` was
  consequently advanced to in_review with AC5 genuinely unmet. Correction was
  applied manually ("Reopened — AC5 measurement was never run (spurious
  finalisation)").

## Desired change

- `git_commit` reports whether a commit was actually created (structured
  result / distinct signal), so `phase_finish` can detect the no-op path
  before the push.
- On the no-op path **without** `--verification-only`: abort before the
  terminal write — item stays open, finish fails loudly with an actionable
  message naming the retained worktree and why, no misattributed commit hash.
- On the no-op path **with** `--verification-only`: finalise as today
  (preserving OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58), but report "no changes / no commit"
  instead of an ambient HEAD.
- `drive`/`phase_parent`: classify a child whose worktree has no attributable
  commit and no verification-only signal as "no work / not finalisable" —
  report and leave open so the parent never advances; keep finish's refusal
  as defence in depth.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_commit` (~2961) commit-vs-no-op
  signal; `git_get_commit_hash` (~3213) attribution; `phase_finish` (~7454)
  refusal + `--verification-only` gating + completion comment wording;
  `_assert_terminal_status` (~707) no-op-path wording; `drive`/`phase_parent`
  (`_classify_child` ~1423, `_has_worktree_changes` ~8798, `_git_path_has_changes`
  ~12099, the drive loop ~9240) classification + reporting.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — existing regression
  pin for the no-op terminal transition; update to assert the gated path and
  add the refusal-path tests.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document `--verification-only` and the no-op
  refusal semantics.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` CLI arg parsing (~12175–12360) — add
  the `--verification-only` flag.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVXU5YWQ004YGZS` — originating work item (this bug, recorded in the llm
  project worklog; moved here because the implement skill source lives in this
  repo).
- `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1`, `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` — the child falsely finalised
  and the parent wrongly advanced to in_review (observed evidence).
- `OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58` — the deliberate no-op-push path for verification-only
  items; its behaviour must be preserved behind the explicit flag.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — regression pin for
  OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58 (terminal status persists on the no-op path).
- Related llm-project items on finish's push/gate correctness (different
  defect surfaces, same file): `LP-0MVTJ2B3H00258U1`, `LP-0MVWY2XQ8005JL0S`,
  `LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0`.
- `SA-0MS8XDUFK004AZ5V` Remove accidentally-tracked .implement_state.json from
  dev — the tracked state file can make a commit-less worktree read as "has
  changes", feeding the false finish; related by find_related.
- `SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV` Reconcile terminal child once finish bound exhausted —
  adjacent drive/finish lifecycle reconciliation; related by find_related.
- `SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG` Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull —
  implement-skill maintenance task; related by find_related.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** tightening `finish` could block a legitimate no-op finalise that an
  operator performs directly (without the flag). Mitigation: the refusal
  message names the exact flag/recovery steps, and the manual-push style
  recovery comment mirrors existing finish failure paths.
- **Risk:** `drive` no longer running finish on a "no work" child could strand
  a genuinely complete-but-uncommitted child. Mitigation: the classifier
  checks for dirty files *and* commits ahead (existing `_git_path_has_changes`
  semantics) and reports the child as "not finalisable" with the worktree
  path, so an agent re-enters and finishes it properly.
- **Assumption:** acceptance *evidence* (prose comments citing operational
  runs) is not a machine-checkable gate; the explicit flag is the gate, and
  evidence stays advisory (producer decision Q2).
- **Scope-creep risk:** follow-ups observed during implementation (e.g.
  reconciling `drive` messaging, flag naming) are recorded as separate linked
  work items, not folded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Default outcome of a no-op finish with no commit attributable to the
  item?" — Answer (producer): **(a) Refuse the terminal write** — finish fails
  loudly, item stays open, finalise requires explicit opt-in. Source:
  interactive reply 2026-11-02. **Recommended: (a)**.
- Q2: "What gates legitimate finalisation of a no-commit item
  (verification-only)? (a) explicit CLI flag; (b) recorded acceptance evidence;
  (c) both." — Answer (producer): **(a) explicit CLI flag** (e.g.
  `--verification-only`), no content heuristics. Source: interactive reply
  2026-11-02. **Recommended: (a)**. Research: evidence comments are prose and
  weak as a hard gate; a flag is deterministic and machine-checkable
  (confirmable in `finish`'s report and tests).
- Q3: "drive/phase_parent treatment of a child whose worktree exists but has
  no commit and no finalise signal? (a) classify 'no work / not finalisable' —
  never run finish, keep open so the parent never advances; (b) keep current
  classification, rely on finish's refusal; (c) auto-detect and re-queue."
  — Answer (producer): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-02.
  **Recommended: (a)** — kills the cascade at the source, with finish's own
  refusal as defence in depth for direct invocations.

Research & evidence (agent):
- Traced the no-op path in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `git_commit`
  returns `True` on a clean tree; `git_get_commit_hash` reports the branch HEAD
  (ambient dev HEAD); no-op push; `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes the
  terminal transition.
- Read `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`: the deliberate
  no-op terminal transition is pinned (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58); tests stub
  `git_commit` green and do not distinguish committed vs nothing-to-commit.
- Verified the installed implement skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`) is a
  byte-identical copy of this repo's `skill/implement/` — this repo is the
  source of truth, hence the item lives here.

# audit: gap-mapped children re-screen in-main-slot and overwrite serviced child audits

## Observed on SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB (epic, all 10 children terminal and on dev)

An epic audit whose **parent** carries one `partial` AC cannot converge while the
default in-main-slot child-audit mode is active. Every run re-screens the same
gap-mapped children, re-blocks on the pending-screens gate, and (worse) overwrites
child audits that a previous session had serviced with real verdicts.

## Root cause (two interacting behaviours)

1. **Gap-mapped children ignore their stored verdict.** In the default
   parent-first flow (`_phase_children`, `audit_children=False`) the
   `not parent_gaps` branch consults `_child_content_changed()` (content-gated
   reuse), but the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch appends the child
   to `pending_children` **without** consulting its stored audit — unlike the
   `--audit-children` P7 pre-pass, which reuses a fresh stored child audit via
   `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and never re-screens it.
2. **In-main-slot mode cannot service screens inside the run.** With
   `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` (default `true`) the gap-mapped child screens are
   emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` and the child audits are persisted as
   `partial` + `main-session review`. A later `persist` pass then **overwrites**
   the previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit with that pending
   `partial` report.

Net effect: service the screens → re-run the parent → the children are re-screened
and their good audits are destroyed → the parent still reports
`Ready to close: No` with `Child screens pending`. The
`<id>.pending-screens.json` signal is never cleared.

## Evidence (this item's run)

| Step | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Audit run 1 | 08:13 | `Ready to close: No`, 7 in-main-slot screens emitted |
| Screens serviced by the session (real file:line evidence) | ~09:55 | 6 children `Yes`, 1 `No` (documented downstream AC) |
| Audit re-run (`--force`, because the stored report was content-fresh) | 10:04 | 14 screens re-emitted; **all 7 child audits overwritten back to `partial` + `main-session review`**; parent `No` with 7 pending screens |
| Screens re-serviced by hand (again) | 10:20 | 6 `Yes` / 1 `No` restored |

The parent's single blocking AC (SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB AC10) is a downstream
verification owned by a **different repository** (`LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X`), so it can
never become `met` on this host — the loop is permanent, not a transient state.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow, a
  gap-mapped child with a content-fresh stored audit is reused (its persisted AC
  verdicts adopted, exactly as the `--audit-children` pre-pass does) and is NOT
  added to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run never persists a
  pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and
  carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** With all children terminal and only one unsatisfiable
  parent AC, a re-run after servicing the child screens reports
  `Ready to close: No` naming **that AC only** (no `Child screens pending` gate),
  and the pending-screens signal is cleared.
- **AC4 — Regression tests** cover both flows (gap-mapped reuse, no overwrite on
  persist) with no real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this (discovered-from).
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling
  (mitigates the reporting side only; it does not stop the re-screen/overwrite).
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — the cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent
  permanently `partial` on this host.

## Problem

Every `audit_runner.py issue <id>` run that finds a medium/low code-quality finding it classifies as a *candidate false positive*:

1. creates a **new** chore work item (`ruff BLE001 in .../implement.py — candidate false positive — producer decision required`), and
2. sets `needsProducerReview = true` on the audited parent item.

Observed during the 2026-11-02 release prep: a backlog of 20+ such chore items accumulated (SA-0MVBD5ZBD007HQZA, SA-0MVI2ZZH9004WGIG, SA-0MVZIKFES006HD99, SA-0MVZK9SBF000HLS2, SA-0MVZL5TE1007YTVJ, SA-0MVZL69QA0007CRJ, ...), and **7 of 36 in_review items** were blocked by the ship skill's producer-review gate purely because of them. Clearing the flag is a manual `wl update` per item and the next audit re-creates another chore + flag, so a release can never converge.

## Expected

- A false-positive candidate should be recorded **once** (deduplicated by rule + file + line + fingerprint), not once per audit run.
- A passing audit verdict (`readyToClose === true`) should clear / not set `needsProducerReview`; the flag should reflect a genuine producer decision, not the existence of an unresolved low-severity lint candidate.
- Consider a documented producer-level suppression (e.g. a per-rule/file allowlist, or an `auditWaiver`) so accepted false positives stop re-surfacing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeated audits of the same unchanged item do not create duplicate chore items (dedupe proven by a test).
2. An audit that ends `Ready to close: Yes` leaves `needsProducerReview` false.
3. An accepted false positive can be recorded once (suppression/waiver) and no longer re-flags the parent.
4. Release gate regression test: a repository with N accepted false-positive chores does not fail the ship producer-review gate.
5. Full suite green.

## Impact

Blocks `/skill:ship release` on repositories with deliberate lint patterns; each release needs manual flag clearing (2026-11-02 release: 7 items cleared by hand).

# Finish gate: report a lagging engine pin when the build fails after `engine:sync`

**Discovered while verifying AC1 of `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) — filed from `MS-0MVZZ767V009KG3F`.**

`SA-0MVZE164P0048306` (completed, `2c81fdd96`) excludes build-originated pin/gitlink churn from the commit and records the composed engine SHA — but only **after a successful build**. A build that *fails* because `engine:sync` advanced the engine past a breaking API change reports a plain compile error with no trace of the advance.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` runs `run_build` → `npm run build`. In this repo `npm run build` starts with `npm run engine:sync`, which advances `./core` to the tracked-branch tip and rewrites/stages `configs/engine-pin.json` when the worktree's pin lags (pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`). If the item's source predates a breaking engine API change, `tsc --noEmit` / `vite build` then compiles the item's source against an engine it was never written for.

Reproduced on tce-main-street in a throwaway worktree at `a6ef0b7d` (pinned `21bedf7a`; engine tracked tip `2305f888`):

```
engine:sync: core updated 21bedf7a8c → 2305f888d0
src/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts(88,5): error TS2353: ... 'hasChoices' does not exist in type 'ContentFieldMapping'.
tests/main-street/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.test.ts(194,44): error TS2551: Property 'hasChoices' does not exist on type 'ManifestNode'. Did you mean 'isChoice'?
npm run build → exit 2
```

Two concrete defects in the failure path (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`):

1. **The advance is invisible.** `engine:sync` logs `core updated <from> → <to>` and the pin rewrite to **stdout**; the build-failure comment posts only `build_result['stderr'][:500]`. The operator sees an unexplained `hasChoices` rename error and cannot tell an engine-induced failure from a source failure.
2. **The data is already there, but unused.** `_build_churn_baseline()` runs *before* `run_build` and captures `gitlinks` (the pre-build `core` gitlink); `_composed_engine_state()` resolves each submodule checkout `HEAD` and compares it with the recorded gitlink. Both are used only on the success path; the failure branch returns before deriving the lag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a build failure, the finish report's build step carries a structured `engine_lag` field with, per advanced submodule: `submodule`, `pinned_sha` (the pre-build recorded gitlink / pin), `composed_sha` (the submodule checkout `HEAD` the failed build compiled against) and `advanced: bool`; the same field appears in the JSON output.
- [ ] The build-failure comment names **both SHAs** and states that the advance is not part of the item's commit, e.g. `build ran against engine <composed_sha>; the item pinned <pinned_sha> — the advance is not part of this item's commit`.
- [ ] The build-failure comment reproduces the build's **stdout** tail (where `engine:sync` logs the advance and the pin rewrite) in addition to stderr, so the `core updated <from> → <to>` line is visible.
- [ ] When the engine did **not** advance during the failed build — or the repo has no submodule — the field is `advanced: false`, the message carries no engine diagnosis, and finish behaves exactly as today.
- [ ] A build that produces no `engine:sync` output at all (Python-only repos, `skipped` build, sync failing before any output) is handled without error.
- [ ] Fixture tests exist and pass in `skill/implement/tests/`, using the hermetic real-submodule fixture pattern from `test_finish_gate_build_churn.py`: (a) a build that advances the engine and then fails names both SHAs; (b) a build that fails without an advance reports no lag; (c) a repo without submodules reports no lag; (d) the failure comment includes the sync line from stdout.
- [ ] `compute_git_state` (cache key, `skill/test_cache.py`) is **unchanged** — no cache-key relaxation.
- [ ] No change to `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (canonical in Tableau-Card-Engine) and no pin-policy change (`CG-0MVO268500071BPI`): this item is **additive reporting only**.
- [ ] `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the new `engine_lag` field and the build-failure note wording.

## Constraints

- Additive reporting only. Do **not** switch the finish gate to a verify-only / pinned-composition `engine:sync` — remedy C was rejected by the producer, and Option B (restore the pin before the build) touches the pin policy and needs explicit producer sign-off. If additive reporting proves insufficient, stop and raise it for sign-off rather than changing build composition.
- No `git add -A` semantics change; the churn exclusion from `SA-0MVZE164P0048306` is untouched.
- All test runs go through the test skill / the finish gate — never an ad-hoc suite invocation.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_build`, the `phase_finish` build-failure branch, `_build_churn_baseline`, `_composed_engine_state`, `_build_churn_refusal_message`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_build_churn.py` — hermetic real-submodule fixture to reuse
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_abort.py` — report-shape and abort-path assertions
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state` (must remain unchanged)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish report and failure-message documentation

## Evidence

- tce-main-street `MS-0MVZZ767V009KG3F` (this gap's origin), `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` (AC1 verification).
- Failing build log: `/tmp/ms0mvtevk8-ac1-probe-build.log`; clean-run probe at `99489ad8`: `/tmp/ms0mvtevk8-ac1-probe.json`.
- tce-main-street recorded limitation: `docs/dev/analysis/ac1-finish-gate-composition-verification.md` — "Observations and limits".

- **SA-0MLYM8EO00SU1RFY** – Move engine adapters wiring into ampa/delegation.py (completed)

## Goal (user story)

*As a framework maintainer*, I need the semaphore's slot-**discovery** rule pinned
by unit tests, so a future semaphore change cannot silently reintroduce the
snapshot-ceiling starvation that stalled a test run for 105 minutes
(SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

`Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` iterates
`range(self.max_workers)` and `flock`s the first free file. `max_workers` is
resolved once in `__init__`, so a waiter created with `max_workers=2` **never
opens slot files `2..7`**, even when they exist in the namespace and are
unlocked. Live evidence (2026-10-31): `/run/user/1000/pi-semaphores/test/` held
slot files `0`-`7`, slots `2,3,4,6,7` were free, and the waiter owned no lock.

This child adds the **failing-first** unit tests only. The implementation is
child "Semaphore: dynamic slot discovery across the namespace", which removes
the strict `xfail` markers added here.

## Scope (tests only)

File: `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` (hermetic — the existing
`_isolate_lock_dir` autouse fixture already points `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` at
`tmp_path`):

- **Discovery:** a waiter constructed with `max_workers=2` against a namespace
  whose slots `0` and `1` are both held, which has already polled at least
  twice, must acquire within the documented bound (one poll interval plus one
  `flock` attempt) once slot files `2..7` are created and left free.
- **Poll cadence:** the documented maximum poll interval is `1.5 x
  _RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS` = 75 ms with jitter enabled and 50 ms with jitter off;
  pin that no attempt sleeps longer than that cap and that a long-waiting
  consumer performs many attempts (`> 3`), not one.
- **Own-ceiling floor:** a waiter never creates slot files beyond its own
  `max_workers` (only `0..1`), even when higher-index slots exist.
- **Late slot observed across many cycles:** create the new slot only after at
  least three poll cycles and assert the waiter still acquires it.

## Constraints

- Tests are hermetic: temporary `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, no host-wide pool, no
  reliance on `/run/user`.
